posts.name: Eva Nambison
posts.cooked:
Dear Sir/ Ma’am,

In the question OPPE_2.4 we students were given a task to create a sed file in which we

  1. Had to drop two Lines of DEBUG, INFO

  2. Had to change the first letter of lowercase to uppercase in message part of the code

  3. Had to change the Date format in the script

As I understood from the tutorial link of the SED part of System Commands from Sayan Ghosh Sir: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i7hIbVWv5K8&t=5052s. The second point given above I tried to change the lowercase of ‘t’ in the word ‘this‘ by using command “s/this/This“ (which you can see in the recorded file for Student’s roll number: 23f2004989) initially and all my public cases were passed but since all private cases were failing again and again I kept on trying different commands with all other changes being correct in my case such as deletion of LEVEL - DEBUG, INFO & changing the Date format and submitted the file. Sir if private cases did contain ‘this‘ as the first letter of message part and the glitch would not have happened students like me who were facing the same problem in question 4 of the OPPE and I would have passed yesterdays exam and so please consider our attempt to solve the question; if the private cases did not contain the word ‘this’ as the first word of the message part in the question please kindly share the reason of the failure of private cases.

Thank you
With regards
Eva Nambison
23f2004989

posts.name: Sayan Ghosh
posts.cooked:
It is nowhere mentioned that messages will start with this, you are to change the first letter of the message to uppercase regardless of what the message is, that is the whole point of using regex in this subquestion.

The correct solution for that subquestion is such:

s/[^) ][^)]+$/\u&/
